title.label: Title: $5,000 Paid for a Fake Rental

content.label:
I wish I had read the reviews about Booking.com BEFORE trusting this company with nearly $5,000 of our money.

My husband and I booked and paid for a two-week vacation at Horizons West in Siesta Key, Florida, through Booking.com back in August. We arrived on October 24, 2026, expecting to begin our vacation, only to discover that OUR RESERVATION DID NOT EXIST!

Someone had used photographs of a real condominium property to advertise a rental they had no authority to rent. The actual condominium management confirmed DIRECTLY TO BOOKING.COM that our reservation was fraudulent and that no such reservation existed in their system. We were also told this wasn’t the first time something like this had happened at that property.

You would think that once Booking.com received confirmation of the fraud, they would immediately step in, take responsibility, and help us find comparable accommodations.

WRONG!

Instead, we received apologies and virtually no meaningful assistance. We were left scrambling to find somewhere else to stay after traveling all the way to Florida.

Even more unbelievable, we were told we needed to provide proof that we stayed somewhere else to obtain a refund. WHY? The actual property had already confirmed that the accommodations we paid for DID NOT EXIST!

We booked through Booking.com because we believed a major, established travel company would verify that the properties advertised on its platform were legitimate. Apparently, that trust was misplaced.

And here’s what concerns me most: Booking.com has an extremely high rating in Apple’s App Store, yet numerous customers on independent review websites describe serious problems with fraudulent reservations, refunds, and customer service.

An app that is easy to navigate means absolutely nothing if you cannot trust the reservations you’re purchasing.

We spent months planning this vacation. Instead of enjoying our arrival, we spent hours dealing with a fraudulent reservation, trying to recover thousands of dollars, and searching for last-minute accommodations.

Booking.com should verify that people actually have the authority to rent the properties they advertise BEFORE accepting thousands of dollars from unsuspecting travelers.

I strongly encourage anyone considering Booking.com to research the company’s customer-service and fraud complaints before booking.

A beautiful app and a five-star rating won’t help you when you arrive hundreds of miles from home and discover that the vacation rental you paid for doesn’t exist.

I WILL NEVER TRUST BOOKING.COM WITH ANOTHER VACATION RESERVATION.

After this experience, I will NEVER book through Booking.com again. I’ve also canceled my reservation for next week because I have absolutely no confidence in this company.

I arrived in Rhode Island late on October 23 for a work trip, only to discover that my hotel could not locate my confirmed reservation.

What followed was an absolute nightmare.

The first Booking.com customer service agent hung up on me. The second left me on the line for over 10 minutes of dead air. By the time the third agent and a supervisor finally attempted to help, I was informed that they could no longer arrange a replacement reservation because it was after midnight.

I spent approximately 45 minutes seeking assistance, and nobody thought to mention this critical deadline until it was too late.

The alternative hotel initially offered was over $500. Although Booking.com offered to price-match, I was expected to pay the full amount upfront on my personal credit card. An unexpected $500+ expense is not a reasonable solution to a failed reservation.

Booking.com eventually issued a refund, but a refund was not what I needed at that moment. I NEEDED A BED.

I ultimately had to find another hotel independently, paying approximately $400 for accommodations I did not secure until around 3 AM. I had to be at a work event by 8:30 AM.

Three agents, a supervisor, nearly an hour of wasted time, and not one workable solution.

I understand that booking errors happen. What I cannot accept is a customer service operation that leaves someone stranded in the middle of the night without meaningful assistance.

I have canceled my upcoming reservation and will not be using Booking.com again. A platform that cannot reliably support travelers when reservations go wrong is not a platform I am willing to trust with future travel.
